To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel variant in the HNF 4A gene in a patient with congenital hyperinsulinemic hyperglycemia and glycogenosis like phenotype.

we have identified a novel heterozytous variant in the HNF1A gene in our patient with congenital hyperinsulinemia and glycogenosis phenotype, and we recommend HNF1A testing in CHI with glycogenosis phenotype before the whole-exome sequencing.
we have identified a novel heterozygotous variant in the HNF-4A gene (LRG_483t.1:c.427-1g>a) in a patient with hyperinsulinism with glycogenosis like phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical and genetic aspects of CHI
the identification of the novel HNF4α variant in a child with CHI and ambiguous glycogenosis phenotype.
the importance of genetic testing in the diagnosis of CHI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenotype of the child is CHI with a glycogenosis-like picture.
the phenotype of the proband and her relatives is caused by a mutation in the HNF1A gene, and not by glycogenosis.
CHI and glycogenic phenotype can be caused by a mutation in HNF4A.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CHI with glycogenosis phenotype is not a glycogenosis and should be considered as CHI with additional glycogenosis phenotype.
CHI may be a part of a broader spectrum of diseases caused by mutations in the HNF genes.
the genetic diagnosis in CHI cases with ambiguous phenotype may be achieved with a limited gene panel testing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HNF4A testing may be considered before WES in selected CHI patients with glycogenosis like phenotype.
the HNF4 gene testing may be recommended in patients with hyperinsulinism with glycogenosis like features.
the HNF4 gene testing should be considered in CHI patients with glycogenosis like phenotype.
